experiments.scope: The sha256-r41-prefix-v1 target with 52-byte messages P || x (P = 20 zero bytes, x the 32-byte chain value, one block), collision of the low 18 bits of the complete digest. Each trial runs ONE attempt of the shipped 7-lane search on the chain f (plan(18): distinguished points with the low 2 bits zero, 92 batches of 7 lanes, cut rule, table, recovery with the same kernel) from a word derived from the trial seed, with no amplification, and returns the two 52-byte messages M(x) and M(y) when the attempt found a pair, two nulls otherwise. The same program also runs the same attempt on an ideal function of the same width (keyed blake2b) and one family-law run with a fresh random 20-byte prefix at n = 10; these are reported as untrusted observations only.
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages are distinct and their complete 41-step digests agree in the low 18 bits (digest bytes 29, 30 and 31, the low 2 bits of byte 29). This is exact: the program recovers a merge of two trails of the chain f at width 18. The number of trials that return a pair is the number of single attempts that succeeded; it is reported as a program check, with the ideal-function control as an untrusted observation, and no probability, interval or sampling inference is drawn from it. Observations (untrusted, the program's own): target_ok, ideal_ok, batches, halts, t1_steps. Not shown: any width-256 cost or success probability.

experiments.scope: The sha256-r41-prefix-v1 target with 52-byte messages P || x (P = 20 zero bytes) at full width 256. Each trial evaluates 448 points x with the shipped packed kernel (source by trial index mod 3: uniform inputs from the seed, counter inputs r + i, iterates of f from 7 seed-derived starts), and returns two distinct points whose complete digests agree in the low 16 bits when the set contains such a pair, two nulls otherwise. Untrusted observations: the numbers of equal pairs in seven 16-bit projections of the digest.
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages M(x) and M(y) are distinct and their complete 41-step digests agree in the low 16 bits (digest bytes 30 and 31). This is exact: it checks the packed kernel and the message construction at full width. The number of returned pairs and the projection counts are reported as program checks, not as estimates, and no inference is drawn from them. Observations (untrusted): source, dup_w0, dup_w3, dup_w7, dup_xor8, dup_sum8, dup_p01, dup_p23. Not shown: collision structure at 2^128 evaluations.
